checklist.setupGuide: Guide: set up your LinkedIn profile
checklist.setupHint: No LinkedIn profile yet? Set it up in this order. The texts (headline, About, positions) come from your draft further down.

account.title: Create the account
account.tip: Sign up with a private email address – not your school, university or employer address, which you will lose later. First and last name as on your CV. In the settings, add a second email address and turn on two-step verification.

quiet.title: Don't share profile updates yet
quiet.tip: While you build the profile: Settings → Visibility → turn off “Share profile updates with your network”, so your network doesn't see every intermediate step. Turn it back on later so that, for example, a new job gets announced.

url.title: Set your own profile URL
url.tip: On your profile, “Edit public profile & URL”: linkedin.com/in/firstname-lastname instead of a string of numbers. Then put the URL on your CV and in your email signature.

location.title: Set location and industry
location.tip: Use the city or region where you want to work as your location – recruiters filter by it. Pick the industry you want to start in.

education.title: Fill in education in detail
education.tip: Without much work experience, education is your strongest section: school or university, degree, field of study, dates – and in the description your focus, thesis and projects. Your draft provides the text.

practice.title: Add internships, jobs, volunteering and projects
practice.tip: Internships and side jobs go under Experience with the matching employment type (e.g. Internship, Part-time). Volunteering has its own “Volunteering” section, study and personal projects go under “Projects”. Add missing sections via “Add profile section”.

openTo.title: Set “Open to” deliberately
openTo.tip: Under “Open to” → “Finding a new job”, enter target roles, locations and workplace type. Then choose who sees it: recruiters only (discreet) or all members (green frame around your photo). Both are common – decide deliberately.

network.title: Make your first connections
network.tip: Connect with classmates and fellow students, teachers and lecturers, colleagues from internships and volunteering – each with a short personal note on how you know each other. A few relevant connections are worth more than many strangers.

follow.title: Follow companies, find alumni
follow.tip: Follow the companies you want to work for. On your school's or university's page, use “Alumni” to find graduates in your target field. One or two thoughtful comments a week make you visible before you post anything yourself.

overview.title: What can {{app}} do?
overview.lead: {{app}} supports every application from job ad to offer. You add a job, the AI rates it against your CV and helps with every step: documents, cover letter, interview, salary.
overview.hint: Open this overview any time via “Help & overview”. Tour per screen: ?

screens.board: All applications as cards, columns = stages.
screens.table: All applications as a sortable table, RAV report.
screens.calendar: Appointments, deadlines and Google Calendar together.
screens.timeline: All activity in time order: what happened when.
screens.profile: Master CV, personal notes, target salary – the basis for all AI texts.
screens.documents: CVs, references, certificates, portfolio – the AI reads their summaries.
screens.cvCheck: Scores your CV out of 100, bullet by bullet.
screens.linkedin: Scores your profile and writes texts to copy over.
screens.letterCoach: Your fixed rules for every cover letter: structure, tone, no-gos.
screens.templates: Google Docs templates for exporting cover letters, CVs and more.
screens.knowledge: Collected knowledge on companies, salaries and interviews.
screens.settings: AI provider, Google, language, profile and security.
screens.setupAi: Step by step: choose a provider, connect, pick a model.
screens.setupGoogle: Step by step: sign in to Google, pick a Drive folder.

search.title: Search
search.body: Filters all applications instantly by company, role, location or tag. ⌘K jumps here from anywhere.

add.title: Add a new job
add.body: Paste a link or the text of a job ad. The AI fills in company, role, workload, work model and location.

columns.title: Columns = stages
columns.body: Each column is an application stage, from inbox to offer. Drag a card to the next column as you progress – the matching tasks appear automatically.

card.title: One application
card.body: The number at the top right is the match score: how well the job fits your CV. A click opens all details.

tabs.title: Four tabs per application
tabs.body: Process: tasks and AI actions of the current stage. Details: fields and job description. Documents: Drive folder. AI: all results at a glance.

process.title: What to do now
process.body: The checklist changes with the stage. In “Preparing letter”, for example, the guided cover-letter assistant appears here.

head.title: Adjust columns
head.body: Drag to reorder, drag the edge for width, click to sort. The column menu shows or hides fields and pins them to the left.

grid.title: Rows
grid.body: A click opens the same details as on the board. AI analyses can be started per row right here.

rav.title: RAV report
rav.body: Creates the monthly proof of job-search efforts for the RAV – as a Google Sheet or CSV.

main.title: Month or week
main.body: Interviews, deadlines and activities from your applications, together with your Google Calendar. Click an event to open the application.

actions.title: Switch view
actions.body: Switch between month and week view and move through time.

main.title: What happened when
main.body: Every change to an application – stage changes, notes, AI results – appears here in time order.

main.title: Archived applications
main.body: Rejected or finished applications end up here with their reason. Open a card to restore it.

actions.title: Cards or table
actions.body: Shows the archive as cards or as a table.

main.title: Your master CV
main.body: Master CV, personal notes and target salary. All AI texts – match score, cover letter, interview – build on it.

focus.title: Your situation
focus.body: Choose school leaver, entry-level or career changer. It decides which help you see – for example the LinkedIn check for entry-level and career changers.

personal.title: Personal details
personal.body: Name, contact, location and headline. They go into cover letters, exports and the RAV proof. Fill them in once.

linkedin.title: Connect LinkedIn
linkedin.body: Optional: with your own LinkedIn developer app, Apply-Pal reads your profile (read-only). It also works without – the LinkedIn check imports a PDF or the ZIP export.

cv.title: Master CV
cv.body: Your CV as text, the most important basis for the AI: match score, cover letter, interview prep. Paste it in “Edit”, check it in “Preview”. The more complete, the better the texts.

notes.title: Personal notes
notes.body: What isn't in the CV: motivation, preferred environment, achievements, things you don't want. The AI uses it for more personal letters.

main.title: Your documents
main.body: CVs, references, certificates and portfolio as links. The AI reads their summaries for every application.

actions.title: Summaries and view
actions.body: The AI summarises every document and reads those summaries for each application. “Summarise all” refreshes them (needs an AI model). On the right you switch between list and tabs.

category.title: A category
category.body: CV, references, certificates, portfolio: each category has its own area. “+” adds a link (Google Doc, Drive PDF or web page) or, for Google Docs categories, creates a new document. CVs here are also the source for the CV check.

main.title: Your CV
main.body: The CV from “Documents” (category CV) shows here as a PDF. None yet? Add it under Documents first. Highlights show which passage a hint refers to.

side.title: Score
side.body: 100 points for impact, presentation and competencies. Hints you deliberately want to keep can be accepted – they then count in full.

tabs.title: Four tabs
tabs.body: Score: overall result and start the check. Improve: bullet by bullet with rewrites. Structure: the detected layout. Versions: compare earlier states.

actions.title: Language and sidebar
actions.body: One CV and one score per language (DE/EN/FR). Show or hide the sidebar here.

main.title: Your profile
main.body: Your imported LinkedIn profile or the draft the AI builds from it. Nothing yet? Import the profile PDF, the ZIP export or copied text under “Source”.

side.title: Step by step
side.body: The recommended path: import, read the score, answer the questions in AI tools and confirm a positioning, generate texts, then work through the checklist. Apply-Pal never writes to LinkedIn itself.

tabs.title: Five tabs
tabs.body: Score: rating. AI tools: choose a positioning and generate texts. Checklist: what to copy to LinkedIn. Versions: compare states. Source: import.

actions.title: Language and view
actions.body: LinkedIn keeps one profile per language. Choose the language here and switch between cards, draft and PDF.

main.title: Rules for every letter
main.body: Structure, values, strengths, phrases and no-gos. These rules go into every cover letter the AI writes.

main.title: Google Docs templates
main.body: One active template per content type and language. Google Doc exports use them automatically.

noGoogle.title: Connect Google first
noGoogle.body: Templates live in your Google Drive. Connect Google under Settings → Integrations (the guided tour “Connect Google” helps).

how.title: How templates work
how.body: A template is a Google Doc with placeholders. On export, Apply-Pal copies it into the application's folder and fills it in. “Import template” picks existing Docs from your Drive.

type.title: A content type
type.body: Cover letter, CV, interview prep, salary and more: each type has its own templates.

lang.title: One active template per language
lang.body: Set one active template for German and one for English. The application's language decides which is used. “Create new” makes an empty template, “From Drive” links an existing one. “Unreachable” means: link it again.

main.title: Collect knowledge
main.body: A company list on the left, collected knowledge on company, salary and interviews on the right.

actions.title: Add a company
actions.body: Create a new company to collect knowledge about it.

main.title: More settings
main.body: Appearance, backup, Drive naming and profile security. Reset the tours at the very top.

ai.title: AI model
ai.body: Without an AI model, match score, cover letters and checks don't work. The guided tour “Set up AI model” in the overview explains each step.

google.title: Google
google.body: Google Drive, Docs and Calendar: for application folders, template exports and appointments. The guided tour “Connect Google” in the overview shows how.

help.title: Help on every screen
help.body: Start this tour again here (or press ?). “Help & overview” in the navigation shows all screens at a glance.

providers.title: 1. Choose a provider
providers.body: Local and free: LM Studio or Ollama – the model runs on your computer, nothing leaves it. In the cloud: Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or OpenRouter with your own API key. Click a provider right here in the bright area, then “Next”.

connection.title: 2. Connection
connection.body: Local: the server address, usually http://localhost:1234 (LM Studio) or http://localhost:11434 (Ollama). The server must be running with a model loaded. Cloud: paste the API key from your provider account – it is stored encrypted.

model.title: 3. Pick a model
model.body: The list shows what your provider offers; for local servers the button next to it reloads it. Empty list = server not running or no model loaded. For cover letters a larger model pays off, e.g. Qwen3 or a current Claude model.

check.title: 4. Check
check.body: If models appear in the list, the connection works. Then start a match score on an application – if a result comes back, you're set.

done.title: Done
done.body: The choice is saved immediately and applies to your profile on every device. API keys stay on the server and are never sent back to the browser.

intro.title: Connect Google
intro.body: One connection for Drive (application folders, exports), Docs (templates) and Calendar (appointments). Apply-Pal only reads what it needs.

connect.title: 1. Sign in
connect.body: “Connect Google” opens Google sign-in (in the desktop app in your system browser). Choose the account, allow access, come back – the status changes to “Connected”. You can click right here.

folder.title: 2. Folder for applications
folder.body: Choose the Drive folder where each application gets a subfolder – with the folder picker or by pasting the folder URL. Without a choice, everything goes to “My Drive”.

next.title: What next?
next.body: Set your Google Docs templates under “Templates” and link CV and references under “Documents”. Pick the calendar further down this page.

settings.title: Help & tours
settings.resetSub: The overview appears again on next start, all tours count as unseen.

ui.driveNotConnected: Google Drive is not connected. Connect it in Settings → Integrations.
